Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.

revision_notes: A single light-check search surfaced a clearly authoritative source (World Bank 'Digital Eswatini' Project Information Document, dated 28 June 2025), which was missed by the original assessment, so the row was escalated from the fast path to full verification. The document reports that Eswatini's cheapest 2GB mobile-broadband basket costs 3.4% of GNI per capita per month, which falls in the 'Moderate (2-5%)' band of the scale — code 3, not code 0.
revised_comments: Eswatini's cheapest 2GB mobile-broadband data plan costs approximately 3.4% of monthly GNI per capita, above the UN Broadband Commission's 2% affordability target though within a moderate range for the region. Fixed-broadband access is markedly less affordable, averaging around 19% of GNI per capita per month.

Definition: Affordability of electricity for residential and small business consumers, measured as cost of electricity relative to income levels. High electricity costs are a direct barrier to ICT adoption and data center viability.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-check search surfaced authoritative, current tariff data from Eswatini's energy regulator (ESERA) and utility (EEC), so the row was escalated to full verification. However, no source publishes electricity cost as a percentage of income directly for Eswatini. Applying ESERA's subsidised 'lifeline' tariff (first 75 kWh/month, approx. E1.40-E1.69/kWh across 2024/25-2026/27) against World Bank GNI per capita (approx. US$3,730, 2025 Atlas method) yields roughly 1.5-2% of monthly income (code 4, Affordable); applying the non-lifeline average domestic tariff (approx. E2.47-E3.14/kWh) to the same consumption yields roughly 3-4% (code 3, Moderate). Because these two plausible, equally defensible assumptions straddle a scale boundary and no authoritative source computes the ratio directly, this is flagged for human review rather than asserting a code.
revised_comments: Eswatini's domestic electricity tariffs are regulated by the Eswatini Energy Regulatory Authority (ESERA), which operates a subsidised 'lifeline' block for the first 75 kWh of monthly consumption (around E1.40-E1.69 per kWh across 2024/25-2026/27) alongside a cost-reflective rate for higher consumption (average tariffs of roughly E2.47-E3.14 per kWh over the same period). Relative to a GNI per capita of around US$3,730, the affordability of a basic monthly bill sits in a moderate-to-affordable range depending on the consumption threshold used.

Eswatini's 2024 EGDI is 0.6081 (rank 113 of 193 globally, improved from 0.4498/rank 141 in 2022), which falls in the 'High' band (0.50-0.64) of the scale — code 3, not code 0.
revised_comments: Eswatini scores 0.6081 on the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI) 2024, ranking 113th of 193 countries globally, an improvement from 141st (0.4498) in 2022. This places Eswatini in the 'High' EGDI band, reflecting gains across the online services, telecommunications infrastructure, and human capital sub-indices.
